method: Direct sequential reading of final current main, before comparison to author coverage inventory; custom source-derived observations, not yet protocol-normalized.

observations.statement: The ordinary-prime minor-arc estimate is derived by integer Vaughan convolution, the same extraction and recombination, and direct total-equidistribution bounds for long and short progressions. Proper prime powers are removed with an explicit error; no unproved Mobius-to-von-Mangoldt transfer is assumed.

Fixed-W affine interpolation uses the polynomial Malcev-coordinate characterization and linear coefficient extrapolation to prove distribution on the full interpolated interval. The W-tricked ideal estimate then applies on the actual progression of modulus Wq, with W-dependent constants.

The centered ray-prime minor-arc bound uses the exact finite character expansion and rational companion bound, absorbing square-root prime-power errors by a lower delta regime. Centered arithmetic progression cancellation is a separate premise.

Quantitative factorization uses Green–Tao factorization and the rational conjugation/commensurable-lattice metric claim. Smooth terms are frozen by right invariance. Haar means are subtracted on each new subgroup quotient. All cells are counted with the original N bound; the factorization exponent is chosen before its polylogarithmic upper exponent, and arbitrary progression savings handle the latter.

The fixed-modulus nilsequence conclusion checks all three factorization hypotheses. Relative inverse transference separately requires the full ordinary-prime pseudorandom measure, including correlation, and the local bounded inverse theorem with its fixed finite family and normalized zero-extension interval norm.

The full majorant construction keeps the smooth cutoff normalization c_chi, a fixed sieve exponent and unit-residue local factors. It verifies cyclic linear forms via convex wraparound regions and correlation including repeated shifts via exceptional-prime weights with all fixed moments. Fixed-factor prime exponents cancel in phi(V)/V; divisor bounds handle the diagonal.
The auxiliary growing cutoff used for linear Gowers replacement is distinguished from the later polynomial cutoff; growth must be sufficiently slow for the fixed-modulus estimates.
